Title: AI Supply-Chain Chokepoints and the Reach of Industrial Policy
Methodology: Herfindahl-Hirschman Index (HHI) across 6 tiers of the global AI stack
Key Findings: Extreme upstream concentration: EUV lithography HHI=10000; CoWoS packaging HHI=8100; Gallium HHI=9804; Graphite HHI=8649. Downstream cloud and models are far less concentrated (HHI 1410 and 1149). Industrial policy cannot replicate full stack domestically.
Limitations: Focuses on US-China dynamics; limited analysis of Global South or Indian industrial policy initiatives

Title: Semicon 2.0 and IndiaAI Mission Drive India's Chip-to-AI Build-Out
Methodology: Administrative data compilation and program audit
Key Findings: Semicon India 2.0 approved July 2026 with ₹127500 crore outlay; 12 projects approved across 6 states (>₹1.64 lakh crore committed); 3 units commercial; C2S in 320 colleges with 68k students; 211 chips taped out; IndiaAI Mission ₹10372 crore outlay with 45000+ shared GPUs; 93.18 lakh subsidized GPU hours used by 237 projects; 20 foundation models selected.
Limitations: Government policy reporting; lacks independent counterfactual econometric evaluation

Title: India's Sovereign AI Status: What It Really Means What's Been Built What's Still Missing
Methodology: Empirical supply chain audit and market pricing survey
Key Findings: India has 34000-45000 subsidized GPUs targeting 100000; compute subsidized at ₹65/GPU-hour (~$0.78/hr); Sarvam 30B and 105B open-sourced (Feb 2026); Bulbul V4 & Sarvam Code. Crucial paradox: 100% of subsidized GPUs are NVIDIA chips (H100/A100) fabricated in Taiwan, creating severe vulnerability to US EAR export controls.
Limitations: Trade publication; qualitative geopolitical assumptions regarding export control risks

Title: Data Centres in India: Sector Report
Publisher: State Bank of India (Project Finance SBU)
Methodology: Field data from 50+ colocation projects and power grid interconnection filings
Key Findings: Installed capacity reached ~1.5 GW in 2025; projected >6.5 GW by 2030; Mumbai accounts for >50% capacity due to undersea cables; rack power density surging to 40-100 kW/rack for AI clusters requiring liquid cooling; Union Budget 2026-27 proposed cloud/AI tax holiday to 2047.
Limitations: Proprietary banking perspective; focus on project bankability rather than national defense resilience

Title: India Data Centre Capacity to Reach 2 GW by 2026
Methodology: Pan-India colocation facility audit and pipeline tracking
Key Findings: Capacity growing to 2000 MW by end of 2026; ₹15.29 lakh crore cumulative investment; Mumbai absorbed 94% of new H1 2026 supply; Tier IV facilities represent 43% of total stock; hyperscalers drive 85% of colocation demand.
Limitations: Commercial real estate focus; excludes compute architecture and chip-level performance metrics

Title: India's Semiconductors and Strategic Dependence: Transition to Indigenous Manufacturing
Methodology: Trade balance analysis and policy synthesis
Key Findings: Evaluates Indian import dependence on Taiwan Korea and Netherlands; details Vikram-32 processor and ATMP facilities; analyzes Union Budget 2026-27 allocations and India Semiconductor Mission (ISM) expansion.
Limitations: Focuses on consumer electronics and legacy microcontrollers; does not model advanced AI accelerators (H100/B200)

Title: World Energy Outlook Special Report: Energy and AI
Methodology: Bottom-up power consumption estimation across 8000+ data centres
Key Findings: Global DC electricity consumption was 415 TWh in 2024 (~1.5% global demand), reaching 945 TWh by 2030. AI search consumes 2.9 Wh/query vs 0.3 Wh for traditional search. Water intensity averages 1.8 L/kWh for evaporative cooling.
Limitations: Aggregated global figures; Indian regional sub-grid transmission bottlenecks not analyzed in detail

Title: United States Data Center Energy Usage Report: 2025 Update
Methodology: Detailed power breakdown: servers (55%), cooling (28%), power conditioning (10%), network (7%). Average PUE is 1.58. High-density AI clusters push cooling requirements to direct-to-chip liquid systems.
Key Findings: US-centric climatic and grid conditions; higher Indian ambient temperatures yield 15-25% higher cooling penalties

Title: Semiconductor Supply Chains AI and Economic Statecraft
Publisher: Centre for Emerging Technology and Security
Methodology: Supply chain node risk mapping and statecraft policy evaluation
Key Findings: Categorizes chokepoints into equipment materials fabrication and packaging. Assesses multilateral weaponized interdependence and economic statecraft mechanisms across allied and non-aligned states.
Limitations: Focuses primarily on UK and Five Eyes posture; secondary treatment of Indian strategic autonomy

Title: The Geopolitics of Compute: Sovereignty Power and Strategic Dependence
Type: Global compute asset mapping and sovereign policy comparison
Methodology: 75% of frontier AI compute clusters reside in the US; 15% in East Asia; under 3% in South Asia. Compute capacity is becoming the primary metric of 21st-century national sovereignty and geopolitical leverage.
Key Findings: Relies on publicly disclosed GPU cluster figures; private intelligence compute excluded

Title: Programmable Sovereignty: Coordinated Specialization as a Response to the N-2 Problem in AI
Type: Game-theoretic and economic modeling of industrial sovereignty
Methodology: Middle powers facing 'N-2' supply chain disadvantages cannot achieve autarkic self-reliance across all technology tiers. Optimal strategy is 'Coordinated Specialization': excelling in strategic niches (e.g. design, packaging, software runtimes) while forming multilateral supply pacts.
Key Findings: Theoretical framework; requires calibration to India's specific fiscal and industrial constraints

Title: Achieving AI Sovereignty: A North-South Coalition for an Alternative AI Stack
Methodology: Proposes Global South compute pooling, open weights architecture, and collective procurement to mitigate reliance on US hyperscalers and Chinese closed systems.
Key Findings: Policy recommendations lack hardware cost-engineering models and data centre PUE validation

Title: NVIDIA AI GPU Market Share 2024-2026: Peak and What Comes Next
Type: Market share regression and bill-of-materials analysis
Methodology: NVIDIA holds 80-87% of AI accelerator revenue. H100 manufacturing cost estimated at $3320 against retail selling price of $27000-$32000. CUDA software ecosystem creates immense developer stickiness.
Key Findings: Forward projections sensitive to hyperscaler internal ASIC adoption (TPU Trainium Maia)

Title: Assessing India's Readiness to Assume a Greater Role in Global Semiconductor Value Chains
Type: Comparative industrial policy and infrastructure readiness assessment
Methodology: India possesses 20% of global semiconductor design workforce and deep EDA expertise, but suffers from capital costs, water infrastructure unreliability, power quality fluctuations, and lack of advanced packaging substrate ecosystem.
Key Findings: Pre-dates Semicon India 2.0 announcement and 2026 fab construction milestones

Title: Thermal Management of Ultra-High-Power AI Accelerators
Publisher: IEEE Transactions on Components Packaging and Manufacturing Technology
Methodology: Rack power densities exceeding 40 kW/rack cannot be cooled with conventional air cooling without exceeding 70°C junction temperatures. Single-phase direct-to-chip liquid cooling achieves thermal resistance <0.03 °C/W with PUE <1.15.
Key Findings: Laboratory bench conditions; does not model monsoon humidity or high ambient Indian summer ambient temperatures (45°C)

Methodology: India peak power demand hit 250 GW during summer 2026 heatwaves. AI data centre power demands in Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu impose localized substation congestion, requiring dedicated captive renewable energy with battery storage (BESS).

Title: Defining the Intension and Extension of Nations' Sovereignty in Generative AI
Methodology: Delineates four distinct layers of technological sovereignty: data sovereignty, compute sovereignty, algorithmic sovereignty, and network infrastructure sovereignty. Highlights sovereignty conflicts under extraterritorial cloud laws (US CLOUD Act).
Key Findings: Legal and political geography focus without quantitative supply chain metrics

Title: Capital Power and Innovation: Global Data Centres Report 2025
Methodology: Identifies powered land availability as the primary rate-limiting step for global data centre expansion. Highlights India as the fastest-growing market in APAC with 22% CAGR.
Key Findings: High-level commercial investment perspective

Title: Global Foundry Revenue Approaches US$53.49 Billion in 2Q26
Type: Quarterly foundry revenue and node tracking
Methodology: TSMC commands >62% total foundry market share and >90% of sub-7nm advanced AI nodes. Advanced packaging capacity (CoWoS) remains booked out through 2027.
